components: kāf-family main-line stem, flatter bowl, and final hook
strokeOrder: flow right to left through the flatter bowl and finish with the pronounced hook without lifting
after one lift, draw the long slash down from the upper right toward the stem
after another lift, draw the shorter floating slash above the first
strokeOrderNote: source-verified independent calligraphic and handwriting animations and prose

strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Pe, gāf, alif, and lām, independent گ calligraphic and handwriting animations and Gāf instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form animations write the kāf-family main-line body first, add the long downward slash after one lift, then add the shorter floating slash above after another lift: three runs separated by two pen lifts. The adjacent prose defines gāf as kāf with a second floating slash, often shorter than the first. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the body-first, three-run order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.

notes: Gāf represents g and differs from kāf by the additional shorter floating slash.
